\section{Claude Cross-Benchmark Analysis}
\label{app:claude_crossbench}

Claude Sonnet~4 serves as negative control on LLMBar (\S\ref{sec:amplification}; Appendix~\ref{app:claude_tost}), but cross-benchmark extension reveals benchmark-dependent style preferences.
Table~\ref{tab:claude_crossbench} reports results across all five tested configurations.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\caption{Claude Sonnet~4 cross-benchmark results. Claude shows no significant style bias on LLMBar but exhibits strong preferences on AlpacaEval and MT-Bench.}
\label{tab:claude_crossbench}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llcccc@{}}
\toprule
Bench & Axis & BT $P$ & Likert $d$ ($p$) & Cat.\ \\
\midrule
LLMBar & Form.\ & .562 & $-$.021 (.721) & --- \\
LLMBar & Verb.\ & .541 & $-$.039 (.743) & --- \\
\midrule
AEval & Form.\ & .840$^{***}$ & .081 (.459) & $\dagger$ \\
AEval & Verb.\ & .750$^{***}$ & --- & --- \\
\midrule
MTB & Form.\ & .850$^{***}$ & .245 (${<}.001$) & $\ddagger$ \\
\bottomrule
\multicolumn{5}{l}{\footnotesize $^{***}$ $p < 0.001$. $\dagger$: Blindspot; $\ddagger$: both sig.; ---: neither.}
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

On AlpacaEval, Claude exhibits a formality Blindspot (BT 84\%, Likert n.s.)---the same pattern observed in all four target judges---and a pure verbosity style effect (BT 75\%; GEE Style OR $= 4.76$, $p < .001$; Orig OR $= 0.87$, n.s.).
On MT-Bench, the formality effect is strong enough for Likert detection (BT 85\%, $d = 0.245$, $p < .001$), consistent with the severity spectrum where Likert sensitivity recovers at large effect sizes.

The benchmark dependence of Claude's negative control status is consistent with the broader pattern: style bias magnitude varies substantially across benchmarks for all judges.
This finding further motivates multi-benchmark evaluation and limits the scope of Claude's negative control to LLMBar.
